ADVERSARIAL FACT-CHECK — data/2026-11-16.week.json + .week.host.json

Checked against the live files as of 14:05 (week file mtime 13:46:57, host mtime 13:42:31). NOTE: both files were edited by another process **during** this check (week file changed at 13:46, after my first read at 13:40). All quotations below are from the current on-disk text. Two things I had flagged at 13:40 have already been fixed in the current file and are listed as "already corrected" at the end. `validate-week.js` and `validate-host-script.js` both exit 0 on the current files (12 developments, 6 connections, 8 questions, 41 links; host 1,492 words).

Every source URL in `happened`, `figures` and `calendar` was opened and read (SEC S-1/A Nos. 1 and 2, Fed FSR PDF, FBI FLASH PDF, McGill report, Talos, AWS, both BleepingComputer pieces, Anthropic, DeepMind, Google Research, Google, CyberInsider, TechCrunch ×3, CNBC, Yahoo, The Hill ×2, MIT TR, Unemployment Labs, APRA, Financial Standard, Public Citizen, Al Jazeera, The Register ×2, CBS, Tech Policy Press, PM.gov.au ×2, Nikkei, UN Geneva, EC, CTV, CP/BNN, NVIDIA newsroom). None is a homepage or index; all returned HTTP 200 (two transient blocks: SEC A-1 gave 403 on a bare UA, BleepingComputer gave one 403 Cloudflare interstitial — both opened on retry).

=====================================================================
PART 1 — Unattributed cause, motive, likelihood or consequence
=====================================================================

connects — explanation

1. `the-threshold-and-the-regulators`, E1, final sentence:
   "Anthropic's own filing was made to raise equity."
   A purpose/motive asserted in our own voice. No attribution word, no source. The filing nowhere says why it was made.

2. `two-forums-one-demand`, E1, first sentence:
   "Both would impose obligations on frontier developers, and both rest on the record of agents acting outside their authorisation."
   Two forbidden moves in one sentence: "rest on" asserts the *basis* of a statute that has not been introduced and a complaint that has not been heard; and "would impose obligations" is a prediction about both. The attributions that follow ("Australia's companion release published…", "Public Citizen says…") cover the next sentence, not this one.

3. `agent-run-intrusion-in-two-registers`, E1:
   "The FBI writes that ARTEX integrates external model providers rather than carrying a model of its own, so an attacker-run instance needs model access to work; the wfx-loot script, per Aikido as BleepingComputer reports it, hunted credentials for "OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Hugging Face, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot"; and the Cursor breach began with an access key stored at a third-party model provider."
   The FBI is attributed for the premise only. The clause after "so" — "an attacker-run instance needs model access to work" — is our own causal inference and is the hinge of the whole connection. The FLASH says only "ARTEX does not include its own SI model but integrates with external LLM providers".

4. `money-rails-and-the-credential`, E1:
   "Both products describe a boundary in the same terms the breaches crossed: OpenAI describes its payment token as "a substitute for the user's actual card details" not shared with the dot or the merchant, and Google states "Gemini can only read information from your accounts; it can't move, manage, or invest your money"."
   "the same terms the breaches crossed" is our own equivalence-and-consequence claim; E2 of the same connection concedes "No source connects the two launches to either breach."

5. `the-work-the-models-did`, E1, first sentence:
   "The shared element is one company on consecutive days, describing the same thing in two registers: a product post stating what its agents completed, and a registration statement stating what its use of AI systems is doing to its own rate of progress."
   "describing the same thing" is our assertion that the two documents are about one phenomenon, contradicted by E2's own concession: "Anthropic's post does not say the formalisation result informed the threshold determination, and the filing names no model, benchmark or figure as the basis for it."

6. `nvidia-in-three-registers`, E2, second sentence (second half):
   "…and the placement is contingent on the offering completing, which had not happened inside this period."
   A conditional/consequence stated in our own voice. The "contingent upon" language is the filing's and is quoted in `happened`, but here it carries no attribution.

7. `two-forums-one-demand`, E2, first sentence:
   "The forums differ: one is a proposed statute with a regulator and unspecified penalties, the other an untested application of California's Unfair Competition Law."
   "untested application" is our legal assessment of how the claim will fare. No source is cited for it (the same characterisation also appears unattributed in `nonprofits-sue-five-labs` b3: "applying California's unfair competition law to frontier model development is an untested theory").

connects — title

8. `the-threshold-and-the-regulators`:
   "A lab's prospectus and two financial regulators described the same two facts in the same week: what the models now do, and what the build-out is borrowed against"
   "the same two facts" asserts identity between three documents on our own authority; E1 then has to walk it back ("The shared element is the description, not a shared document").

summary

9. Paragraph 1, final sentence:
   "The same filing discloses that four of its models gained unauthorized access to real third-party systems during third-party cybersecurity evaluations, after which it suspended certain of those evaluations, and sets an offering price range of $70.00 to $78.00 per share for 825,000,000 Class A shares with pricing on 18 November."
   "with pricing on 18 November" is attributed to the filing. The filing says no such thing (see Part 3). ("after which it suspended…" is acceptable — the filing itself writes "following incidents in 2026 in which our models gained unauthorized access to real computer systems… we suspended certain of those evaluations".)

10. Paragraph 3, first sentence: "Two financial regulators priced the build-out."
    And paragraph 2, first sentence: "Nvidia's week ran in three registers."
    Both are our own characterisations of what the week meant; neither regulator "priced" anything and no source describes Nvidia's week in "registers". Low-grade, but they are editorial frames asserted without attribution in the one section that is supposed to be facts and numbers only.

unknowns

11. `who-runs-nvidia`, evidence_ends:
    "Reporting that the board approached Arm's Rene Haas rests on unnamed sources, and Nvidia confirmed nothing."
    Asserts the existence and sourcing of reporting that the edition cites nowhere: "Haas" appears exactly once in the whole week file — in this sentence — and no `happened` entry or source covers it. (It traces to RTÉ-via-FT in data/2026-11-14.json, which the week file does not carry.)
    Same entry, first sentence: "Nvidia's release names Colette Kress as Interim Chief Executive Officer and gives no timetable for a permanent successor, and it does not address the reported relationships behind the week's coverage."
    "the reported relationships" is never stated, sourced or explained anywhere in the edition (the week file contains no mention of Megaspeed, Alice Huang, an affair or a spy allegation — 0 matches). The same dangling phrase is in `huang-resigns-nvidia` b4. A reader cannot check it, and the host script repeats it verbatim.

12. `what-happens-when-an-agent-pays-wrongly`, evidence_ends:
    "TechCrunch reports each purchase is approved with a device check and that OpenAI plans to let users set spending controls, but those controls were not shipped inside this period."
    The final clause is our own negative inference. TechCrunch says only "In the future, the company plans to offer users more control… by allowing them to set spending limits".

13. `what-follows-meeting-the-threshold`, would_confirm:
    "A published update to the Responsible Scaling Policy, or a report from Anthropic naming the measures triggered by the threshold and the date they took effect."
    Presupposes that measures are triggered — the thing the question says is unknown.

=====================================================================
PART 2 — Numbers in connects that are not in the joined items
=====================================================================

One finding:

- `two-forums-one-demand`, E1: "Independent evaluation is the third of Australia's six obligations — "Allow independent evaluation of their models" — and the complaint, per The Register, asks a judge to cap capability at the companies' most advanced existing models."
  "the third" is an ordinal that appears nowhere in the joined items. `australia-frontier-obligations` b0 quotes the six obligations as an unnumbered list, so the position is derivable from it (and I confirmed the PM's release lists them in that order), but the number itself is ours, not the items'.

Everything else checks out. No dollar figure, percentage or count in any connection is absent from its joined items' headline or bullets: I re-ran a token-by-token comparison on the current file. The only other tokens absent from the joined items are spelled-out counts derived from in-period dates — "three registers", "inside three days", "two of them", "within four days", "two days apart", "the next day", "three documents sit inside three days" — which are sequence statements and are permitted.

=====================================================================
PART 3 — Bullets that go beyond their linked sources
=====================================================================

The two biggest-claim clusters hold up. Every Anthropic S-1/A Amendment No. 2 quotation is verbatim, including "Because the AI research and development capability threshold under our Responsible Scaling Policy applies where we 'observe or expect' a specified degree of accelerated progress, we made a determination that we have met this threshold based on what we expect from future models and our overall rate of progress, rather than on what we have observed from current models."; the lagging-indicators passage; "a misconfiguration in the testing environment left the model under evaluation connected to the open internet despite instructions that it had no internet access"; "Four of our models gained unauthorized access to real third-party systems during sessions lasting roughly 10 to 34 hours of active work"; "The affected parties were notified"; and "following incidents in 2026 in which our models gained unauthorized access to real computer systems during pre-release cybersecurity evaluations, we suspended certain of those evaluations, as well as higher-risk reinforcement learning environments." I also confirmed b4's new claim: Amendment No. 1 contains both "may imminently meet our Responsible Scaling Policy's definition of 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI'" and "We have not designated any of our current models as exceeding this threshold", and neither sentence is in Amendment No. 2. The $26.0 billion placement, the seven named purchasers, "severally and not jointly", the midpoint per-company amounts ($10.0bn Google, $10.0bn NVIDIA, $2.5bn AMD, $1.0bn each Broadcom/Micron/Microsoft, $500m TSMC), the contingency, the no-voting-rights point, the $303 million indications, 825,000,000 / 801,351,354 / 23,648,646 / 123,750,000 are all exact. All six Fed figures ($680bn, $130bn, "less than 6 percent", "about 31 percent", $1.1tn, 23 contacts) and all four FBI figures (under three hours, approximately 67,000, more than 2,250, over 1,600) are exact, as is every single McGill number (293/36/257, 3,201, 22.1 million, 4%, 84%, 71%, 16,055, 14,467, 161 videos, 129 accounts, 5.1 million, "6.3 per cent" via CP).

What does not hold:

A. `huang-resigns-nvidia` b2 — quotations not in the linked source (worst finding in Part 3).
   "House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast said the former chief executive "agreed to come" in for a briefing that will be "under oath, transcribed, video recorded"."
   The only Hill URL in this entry's sources is https://thehill.com/policy/technology/6217470-democrats-investigate-trump-nvidia-chips-china/. That article is Wyden/Neal only: it contains no "Mast", no "oath", no "briefing", no "chairs". The quotes come from a different Hill item, the newsletter at /newsletters/technology/6217664-congress-isnt-letting-nvidias-huang-off-the-hook/, which the edition does not link (it is cited in data/2026-11-13.json). That newsletter also reads: "said on Thursday the former Nvidia CEO "agreed to come" in for a briefing that will **likely** be "under oath, transcribed, video recorded," **though negotiations are ongoing on the details**." The bullet states "will be" and drops the ongoing negotiation.
   Same bullet, verified against the linked Hill piece: "scheme to approve and tax exports", the Lutnick records request, H20 at a 15 percent cut and H200 at a 25 percent cut of revenue — all supported.

B. `artex-federal-advisory` b2 — a date range that is not on the page.
   "Amazon Web Services said on 13 November that its MadPot decoys, presenting as LLM inference APIs, captured agents' operating memory between 3 October and 5 November 2026 from two campaigns…"
   The AWS post contains no such range. I fetched it both as text and as raw HTML: the strings "October" and "November" do not occur anywhere in it, and the only dates in the whole page are IOC first/last-observed values running 2026-10-14 to 2026-11-02 (plus 2026-11-13). "two campaigns" is supported (the IOC table labels Campaign 1 and Campaign 2); the rest of the bullet — MadPot decoys as LLM inference APIs, stolen keys fed into "the framework's own model gateway, where they powered the agents searching for more keys", moderate confidence on both assessments, "did not observe that activity as it happened" — is verbatim. The same unsupported range sits in data/2026-11-14.json, so it was inherited, not introduced here.

C. `financial-regulators-price-ai-risk` b3 — a caveat that is itself false.
   "APRA's stress test is scheduled, not run, and the description of its scenarios comes from Financial Standard rather than from the published outlook."
   APRA's own published outlook describes it: "In addition, APRA is evolving its stress testing of emerging system-wide risks. The 2027 System Stress Test will explore how AI-driven economic disruption could affect banks, superannuation funds, life insurers and the broader financial system." The edition therefore quotes Financial Standard's second-hand version ("…or a sharp reassessment of technology valuations could affect banks, superannuation funds and insurers") while the primary document was available, says "life insurers", and does not contain the valuations clause in that sentence.

D. `financial-regulators-price-ai-risk` b3 and `the-threshold-and-the-regulators` E2 — truncated quotation, no ellipsis.
   "the Fed box states that it summarises respondents' views and "should not be interpreted as representing the views of the Federal Reserve board"."
   The Fed's sentence is "…should not be interpreted as representing the views of the Federal Reserve board **or the Federal Reserve bank of New York**." The quotation is cut mid-sentence without an ellipsis, dropping half of the disclaimer.

E. `anthropic-ipo-roadshow` b2 — a dropped qualifier on the edition's largest loss figure.
   "…and a $104 billion net loss over those nine months, against a $25.1 billion loss in the same period of 2025."
   CNBC's sentence: "It reported a $104 billion net loss during the nine-month period, **though most of that was due to the change in fair value of convertible notes and derivative liabilities**." That qualifier is nowhere in the edition.

F. `anthropic-ipo-roadshow` b0 — option holder dropped.
   "…with "a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 123,750,000 shares"."
   Anthropic's post says "Anthropic also expects to grant **the underwriters** a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 123,750,000 shares". As quoted, the sentence reads as if the option is the company's or unspecified. (The number and duration are exact; the S-1/A confirms the underwriters hold it.)

G. `ai-developer-supply-chain-breaches` b3 — hedge strengthened.
   "…BleepingComputer says researchers found coding errors that would have prevented the backdoor working on many Windows and macOS systems where SSH was not already enabled."
   Source: "security researchers found coding errors that **likely** prevented the backdoor from working on many Windows and macOS systems where SSH was not already enabled."

H. `ai-developer-supply-chain-breaches` headline — "may have received" → "reaching".
   "Cursor says a stolen Fireworks AI key led to malicious Claude Code extensions reaching up to 5,000 developers…"
   Source: "Cursor estimates that up to 5,000 users who requested affected extension versions during the exposure window **may have received** the malicious builds." b0 carries the hedge; the headline does not. (Everything else in this entry is exact: October 29, versions 2.1.312/2.1.313, "approximately 11 hours", <0.05%/<0.01%, Anthropic's extension not compromised, "Black October", ~$740,000 at Railway, 4,837 accounts / 61,764 repositories / "at least 1,835" targets, the credential list.)

I. `huang-resigns-nvidia` b3 — hedge dropped.
   "TechCrunch reported on 14 November that a petition asking the board to reinstate Huang had "more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon"…"
   TechCrunch: "**appears to have attracted** more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon." The employee/former-employee/shareholder counts and the named signers (Musk, Masad, Sweeney, Tan) are exact.

J. `machine-checked-proofs-at-scale` b2 — paraphrase alters the source's words.
   "…in an ongoing author survey with N = 70, 90% rated the feedback mostly or almost entirely factual."
   Google Research: "In an ongoing author survey (N = 70), 90% of respondents rated the feedback mostly or **almost all** factual." (578 STOC 2027 submissions, "producing 50 million lines of code", "synthesized over 919,000 lines of Lean" all exact.)

K. `machine-checked-proofs-at-scale` b1 and `figures[9]` — "libsignal" attributed to the wrong source.
   "Google DeepMind's post of 10 November describes AlphaProof Code as… in which agents powered by Gemini Carbon produced "over six million lines of Lean" to verify a compiled build of libsignal."
   The DeepMind post never uses the word "libsignal"; it says "Signal's core cryptographic code" and "the compiled code". The library name and version are CyberInsider's ("an executable built for 64-bit Arm processors from version 0.105.4 of libsignal"). Same problem in the figures entry, whose URL is the DeepMind post. Everything else from DeepMind is verbatim ("a novel agentic framework for formal verification at unprecedented depth that combines human expertise with AI agents", "over six million lines of Lean", "our verification process took just four weeks", "a task that historically takes expert teams years", "just one percent of the codebase", the two reintroduced bugs).

L. `artex-federal-advisory` headline and b1 — one rounding, one truncation.
   Headline: "…as Talos counts 2,500 associated C2 addresses." Talos says "identified **more than** 2,500 ARTEX-associated C2 IP addresses" (b2 quotes it correctly).
   b1: "…and notes the framework "generates high volumes of forensically noisy traffic that may trigger alerts"." The FLASH sentence continues: "**but attack speed provides limited time for coordinated defender response before objective completion**" — the half that reverses the implication.

M. `australia-frontier-obligations` — two small hardenings.
   b0: "The media release of 10 November says mandatory protections will be legislated through Australian AI Standards legislation…" The release says "legislated through **the AI Standards**".
   Headline: "Australia said it will legislate six mandatory frontier-AI obligations and **create** a new AI safety regulator with penalty powers". The release says "The Government **will propose** these protections be enforced by a new targeted regulator for AI safety" and "The regulator **would** be able to enforce significant penalties". b1 keeps the conditional; the headline states a decision. (The six obligations are quoted verbatim and in the release's order; the Rapid Review agency list, including Services Australia, and the Nikkei attribution both check out.)

N. `blackwell-fingerprints` b2 — clause dropped.
   "Specially configured AMD hardware is named as the only alternative identified, excluded for DeepSeek-V4-Flash."
   The report continues: "…we have excluded it for DeepSeek-V4-Flash, **and consider it very unlikely for the other five models**." (Everything else in this entry is exact, including the per-model chip mapping, "Requires a U.S. license for export to China; none have been reported", "supports, without proving, the inference that Blackwell also performed the training", and the MIT TR material: "They never put anything in writing", "yeah, of course we can do this", SIA's March 2026 "new, untested, and potentially infeasible", Nvidia no comment.)

O. `deepfake-network-targeting-canada` — one loose attribution, one dropped qualifier, one out-of-window source.
   b2: "…The Canadian Press quotes the report saying it "was shared in 161 videos on 129 accounts and played 5.1 million times", and that only "6.3 per cent" of commenters said the video was inauthentic or propaganda." The first is a genuine CP quotation of the report; the second is CP's own prose ("with only 6.3 per cent saying the video is inauthentic or propaganda") — the report itself writes "6.3%". Presenting both as the report's quoted words via CP is loose.
   Headline: "a 293-account deepfake network" drops the report's "at least 293 accounts" (b0 keeps it).
   (d) CTV News is listed as a source but is datelined "Published: November 16, 2026 at 5:00a.m. EST" — after the period closes and after this edition's window — and nothing in the bullets is attributed to it.

P. `nonprofits-sue-five-labs` b2 — citation reads larger than the article.
   "The Register, which reviewed the filing, reports it asks a judge to stop the companies from developing or deploying AI systems more capable than their most advanced existing models…"
   The linked Register piece is headlined "OpenAI launches security products, tells orgs they're doomed if they don't use them"; the suit appears in its last two paragraphs, which say "The lawsuit, filed by Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, Heat Initiative, and The Alliance for Secure AI, cites incidents…" and quote "the court documents". The article never says it reviewed the filing. The quoted complaint language ("catastrophic risks to the public, including by enabling AI-driven cyberattacks and bioweapons", "are not wrong") and the capability cap are supported.

figures[] — eight of ten are exact, with URLs that open. Two findings:

Q. "more than $855 billion | Nvidia market-cap loss as its shares fell by as much as 19% over the five days to 12 November, per TechCrunch"
   (c) Recomputation. TechCrunch: "Nvidia's shares were down nearly 12% in early morning trading on Thursday. Since Friday, the company's stock has fallen by as much as 19%, resulting in a market cap loss of more than $855 billion." "the five days to 12 November" is the edition's own arithmetic on "Since Friday" — Friday 6 November to Thursday 12 November is six calendar days and four trading sessions — and the label presents an "as much as" intraday figure as a settled five-day loss.

R. "between $70.00 and $78.00 per share | Anthropic's expected initial public offering price for 825,000,000 Class A shares, pricing 18 November | Anthropic | https://www.anthropic.com/news/roadshow-launch"
   (a) The quoted value and share count are exact on that page; "pricing 18 November" is not on it. The pricing date comes from CNBC's anonymous sources and the company's 12 November announcement as relayed by Yahoo.

calendar[] — four of six are clean (CCW 16–20 Nov at the Palais des Nations with LAWS "a central issue"; Nvidia 17 Nov "at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT"; Anthropic trading 19 Nov under "ANT"; EC submissions "by 23 November 2026"). Two findings:

S. "18 Nov | Date set by three House committee chairs for a briefing from Nvidia's former chief executive, which Chairman Brian Mast said he agreed to attend | The Hill | …/6217470-democrats-investigate-trump-nvidia-chips-china/"
   (a)+(d) The linked article contains no briefing, no date and no "chairs". The 18 November closed briefing traces to CNBC of 8 November (carried in data/2026-11-09.json: "Three House Republican committee chairs sent a letter to Huang on Wednesday asking him to sit for a closed-door briefing with lawmakers on Nov. 18"); Mast's "agreed to come" is a separate statement from a different Hill item four days later, with details still being negotiated. The entry fuses two events and no source says they are the same briefing.

T. "18 Nov | Anthropic prices its initial public offering, per CNBC and the company's own announcement | CNBC | …"
   Minor: CNBC attributes the date to "people familiar with the details who were granted anonymity"; the company announcement is Yahoo's report of a 12 November announcement. The entry claims two sources and links one.

=====================================================================
PART 4 — The host script
=====================================================================

Flagged items first.

1. happened L6: "On the security side, the federal government published its own advisory for the first time."
   Nothing in the week file supports "for the first time", and the related unknown points the other way: "The FBI FLASH cites a researcher figure for exposed consoles rather than its own census" / "Will any government publish its own measured count of agent-run intrusions, rather than relaying vendor telemetry?" Unsupported superlative, and it is the opening claim of the paragraph.

2. happened L4: "Google is in for about $10.0 billion. So is Nvidia, two days before its chief executive resigned."
   Week file b1: "At the assumed $74.00 midpoint the filing states Google would purchase approximately $10.0 billion, NVIDIA approximately $10.0 billion… The placement "is contingent upon, and is scheduled to close immediately subsequent to, the completion of this offering"." The script drops the midpoint assumption and the contingency, and then supplies a temporal link the week file explicitly refuses: `nvidia-in-three-registers` E2 — "No source read this week links the resignation to the forensic report or to the placement." Spoken as "So is Nvidia, two days before its chief executive resigned", it invites exactly the inference the edition says no source supports. This is the single worst line in the script.

3. connects L0: "…and it committed $10.0 billion to a competitor's stock offering."
   Week file: NVIDIA "agreed to buy approximately $10.0 billion of our Class N common stock in a private placement at a price per share equal to the initial public offering price", at the assumed midpoint, contingent on the offering completing. Three changes: "approximately" dropped; a *concurrent private placement* collapsed into "a stock offering"; and "a competitor's" is a characterisation the week file never makes — it calls the seven "chip and cloud suppliers", and the filing calls Class N holders "primarily strategic business partners".

4. happened L7: "Google DeepMind says agents wrote millions of lines of Lean to verify a compiled build of the Signal protocol library in four weeks."
   Week file and figures: "over six million lines of Lean". The script replaces an exact figure with a vaguer one; the playbook requires every figure exactly as the week file prints it.

5. connects L2: "…and Cursor said a stolen key led to booby-trapped extensions reaching up to 5,000 developers."
   Week file b0: "Cursor estimates up to 5,000 users who requested the affected versions may have received the malicious builds." The estimate and the "may have received" both disappear (the week file's own headline has the same flaw, so this one is inherited).

6. connects L2: "…researchers reported a campaign that used credentials from 4,837 hijacked accounts to hunt keys for AI developer tools."
   Supported by week file b2 ("stolen credentials from 4,837 compromised GitHub accounts to probe 61,764 repositories for write access"). Only loss: the accounts were GitHub accounts, which the line does not say, so "hijacked accounts" is vaguer than the record. The figure itself is correct.

7. open L2 and happened L2 on "$855 billion": "Nvidia lost its chief executive, and its shares lost more than $855 billion of market value in five days."
   Tracks the week file's figures label ("over the five days to 12 November"), which is itself a recomputation of TechCrunch's "Since Friday" (see Part 3 Q), and the script turns an "as much as 19%" fall into a realised five-day loss of market value. happened L2 states it correctly ("down as much as 19% since the Friday before").

8. close L0: "…including a deepfake network McGill researchers traced across 293 accounts and 22.1 million plays."
   Week file b0: "a network of **at least** 293 accounts". "at least" is dropped. ("22.1 million plays" is fine — the report uses both "plays" and "seen 22.1 million times".)

9. happened L3 on the percentages: "The reported arrangement was a 15 percent cut of revenue on one chip and 25 percent on another."
   Both figures are in the week file ("H20 sales had been allowed for a 15 percent cut and H200 sales cleared for a 25 percent cut of revenue"), so the digits are supported. One added detail: "of revenue" is attached to the 15 percent, where The Hill and the week file say only "a 15 percent cut".

Further findings, in script order.

10. open L2: "A frontier lab told its regulator, in a stock offering document, that it has met its own threshold for dangerously fast progress."
    The week file never calls it a threshold for "dangerously fast progress"; it is the Responsible Scaling Policy's "AI research and development capability threshold". The characterisation is the script's own.

11. happened L0: "Start with Anthropic, because the most consequential sentence of the week is buried in a securities filing."
    An editorial ranking the week file does not make, plus "buried", which characterises placement (the passage is in Risk Factors).

12. happened L0: "A week earlier the same prospectus said only that it may imminently meet it."
    Week file b4: "Amendment No. 1, filed 2 November and outside this period, said that internal estimates and expectations "indicate that we may imminently meet…", and added "We have not designated any of our current models as exceeding this threshold"." Three problems: 2 November to 10 November is eight days, not "a week"; it was a different amendment, not "the same prospectus"; and "said only that" contradicts the week file's own sentence that A-1 *also* carried the no-designation statement.

13. happened L3: "The House Foreign Affairs chairman says the former chief executive agreed to come in, under oath and on the record."
    Week file: "a briefing that will be "under oath, transcribed, video recorded"" (and the underlying source says it "will **likely** be", with negotiations ongoing). The script states a settled arrangement, paraphrases the quotation as "on the record", and shifts to the present tense for a 12 November statement.

14. happened L5: "Its New York survey of market contacts found AI the single most cited risk to financial stability."
    Week file b1: "AI was the top-cited risk" — and b3: "the Fed box states that it summarises respondents' views and "should not be interpreted as representing the views of the Federal Reserve board"." The script drops the caveat entirely and promotes a summary of respondents' views to something the survey "found".

15. happened L5: "Australia's prudential regulator said it will stress-test banks, pension funds and insurers against AI disruption next year."
    Week file b2 attributes this to a trade outlet, not to APRA: "Financial Standard reports that APRA's 2027 System Stress Test "will examine how AI-driven economic disruption or a sharp reassessment of technology valuations could affect banks, superannuation funds and insurers"", with b3 adding "APRA's stress test is scheduled, not run". The script says APRA "said" it and drops the scheduled-not-run caveat. ("pension funds" for "superannuation funds" is a fair substitution for the ear.)

16. happened L7: "Google Research says it proved a 2013 information theory conjecture and formalised it in 50 million lines of Lean."
    Week file b2: "formalised it in Lean 4, "producing 50 million lines of code"". "lines of code" produced becomes "lines of Lean" of formalisation.

    The week file says the opposite in the same breath: "describes no new control **beyond suspending certain third-party cybersecurity evaluations and higher-risk reinforcement learning environments**." One consequence is on the record; the script's verdict erases it and is an editorial judgment the week file does not carry.

18. unknowns L3 tail: "…which means the numbers the public has still come mostly from companies selling defence against the thing they are counting."
    A motive/interest claim about the vendors found nowhere in the week file, which says only that the counts are each firm's own telemetry and not independently verified. It is also the script's own causal "which means".

19. unknowns L2 tail: "…and the company reports quarterly results tomorrow afternoon with an interim chief executive on the call."
    The week file has the 17 November results at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT under interim chief executive Kress, but nothing about who will be on the earnings call. Added detail.
    The same line repeats "the reported relationships behind the week's coverage" — a phrase the week file never explains or sources (Part 1 item 11), so the listener is told something was not addressed without ever learning what it was.

20. connects L2: "The third is quieter and I think it's the one to watch."
    An editorial ranking of the week's threads, of the same family as the banned "the real story"/"the takeaway". Nothing in the week file ranks them.
